<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: 

close #30429
close #29685
close #30362

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

Encoding:
- `Encoding` is changed to an interface. Implementations includes `EncodingUTF8`, `EncodingASCII`, `EncodingLatin1`, `EncodingBin` and `EncodingGBK`.
- `StringValidator` is merged to `Encoding`. `Encoding.Validate` is the new interface.
- `NewEncoding()` is renamed to `FindEncoding()` since there is no memory allocation anymore.
- One more value `nSrc` is returned from `Encode`/`Decode` to indicate how many source bytes are consumed. This is useful in truncation.

Binary Literal Handling:
- The built-in functions are classified into 3 kinds of `funcProp`(function property):
  - `funcPropNone`: No property. The arguments are not specially handled.
  - `funcPropBinAware`: The function depends on the binary representation of its string arguments. It will wrap each argument with `to_binary()`.
  - `funcPropAuto`: There are mulitple string arguments. Implicit cast can happen. It will wrap `to_binary()` or `from_binary()` according to charsets.
- All the string-related functions are considered.

Built-in functions:
- Invalid string characters are handled properly.
- builtinCharSig(`char()`): it only returns null for invalid strings when the SQL mode is strict.
- builtinConvertSig(`convert()`): it reuses the charset.Encoding.
- builtinBitLengthSig(`bit_length()`): the special encoding is implemented through warping `to_binary()`.
- builtinOrdSig(`ord()`): it fallbacks to using the first byte instead of returning encoding error for invalid strings.
- Encoding field is removed from `lowerFunctionClass` and `upperFunctionClass` without performance loss.

### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [ ] Unit test
- [x] Integration test
- [ ] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
- [ ] No code

Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory
- [ ] Breaking backward compatibility

Documentation

- [ ] Affects user behaviors
- [ ] Contains syntax changes
- [ ] Contains variable changes
- [ ] Contains experimental features
- [ ] Changes MySQL compatibility

<!-- bugfix or new feature needs a release note -->


issue_context.title: builtin func char() has different result between MySQL when value is illegal UTF8 character
comments:
We didn't check the param for `char()` is UTF8 character or not. And we should check it. The `convert` also has same problem. Seems if builtin functions support `using utf8`, they will have same problem.

code
```
drop table if exists t;
create table t (a binary(20));
insert into t values (0x1e240);
select convert(t.a using utf8) from t;
```

result which should be `NULL`
```
mysql> select convert(t.a using utf8) from t;
+-------------------------+
| convert(t.a using utf8) |
+-------------------------+
| �@                      |
+-------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```
Please check whether the issue should be labeled with 'affects-x.y' or 'fixes-x.y.z', and then remove 'needs-more-info' label.
